shared_elements: upright freestanding carved stone monument (stela/pillar) set in a landscape
relief carving on a broad flat vertical face
horizontal band of repeated small motifs crossing the surface
animal or creature figures in profile
rough stone/ground at the base of the monument
justification: Both are tall upright carved stones bearing relief imagery organised with a horizontal banded division and profile creatures plus disc forms, and both are shown standing amid rubble in the open, which gives a superficial family resemblance. But A is a densely packed, deeply undercut, curvilinear composition built around a single frontal human figure filling the whole field, while B is a sparse, shallow, flat-surfaced arrangement of isolated animal motifs on largely blank stone — the manner of carving and the compositional logic are quite different.
